explanation: Position Independent Code (PIC) is a code generation technique that allows code to be loaded and executed at any memory address without modification.  This is crucial for shared libraries (like .so files on Linux or .dll files on Windows) because multiple processes might load the same shared library into different memory locations simultaneously. The Global Offset Table (GOT) is a data structure used by PIC code to resolve addresses of global variables and functions at runtime.  The loader initializes the GOT entries with the actual memory addresses during loading, enabling the PIC code to access these addresses regardless of its own load address.
keywords: PIC, GOT, Global Offset Table, Dynamic Relocation
